question: Should nix-openclaw keep requiring external runtime plugins such as ByteRover to publish a reproducible dependency closure, or add a new supported composition/package-resolution path for plugins that do not meet that requirement?
rationale: The existing restriction is deliberate and protects deterministic Nix builds, while relaxing it or exposing composable raw paths would establish new user-facing packaging and configuration policy.

options.title: Keep reproducible-source boundary
options.body: Require ByteRover to publish a bundled or shrinkwrapped artifact and add concise setup guidance once that artifact works through `runtimePluginSources`.

options.title: Add composable external paths
options.body: Design a declarative option that merges user-supplied plugin roots with catalog outputs while retaining one generated `plugins.load.paths` owner.

options.title: Support additional npm lock shapes
options.body: Extend the package builder to resolve another immutable dependency format, with focused reproducibility and offline-build coverage.

recommendation.title: Keep reproducible-source boundary
recommendation.body: Require ByteRover to publish a bundled or shrinkwrapped artifact and add concise setup guidance once that artifact works through `runtimePluginSources`.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from recent plugin-artifact packaging history and direct issue involvement.
